title: Reading an HTTP Exchange
contentMd:
Every time a browser or app talks to a server, it speaks HTTP. The client sends a request that names a method, a path, and sometimes a body. The server replies with a status code and a body of its own. Learning to read this exchange is the first skill of any backend engineer.

The method tells the server what to do. GET asks for data, POST creates something new, PUT replaces a resource, and DELETE removes it. PATCH changes only part of a resource. Choosing the right method makes your API predictable for everyone who consumes it.

The status code is the server's one-line verdict. Codes in the 200 range mean success, the 400 range means the client made a mistake, and the 500 range means the server failed. A quick look at the code often tells you where to start debugging.

Headers carry metadata about the request and the response. Content-Type says what format the body uses, while Authorization carries the caller's credentials. Mastering these fundamentals makes the rest of backend work far easier.
contentCn:
每当浏览器或应用与服务器通信时，说的都是 HTTP。客户端发出一个请求，其中指明方法（method）、路径（path），有时还带一个请求体（body）。服务器则回以一个状态码（status code）和属于它自己的响应体。学会读懂这一次往返，是任何后端工程师的第一项基本功。

方法告诉服务器该做什么。GET 用于获取数据，POST 用于创建新东西，PUT 用于替换某个资源，DELETE 用于删除资源，PATCH 只修改资源的一部分。选对方法，你的 API 对每一个使用它的人来说都可预期。

状态码是服务器给出的一行判决。2xx 段表示成功，4xx 段表示客户端出了错，5xx 段表示服务器失败。扫一眼状态码，往往就告诉你该从哪里开始排查。

头部（header）承载着关于请求与响应的元信息。Content-Type 说明请求体采用什么格式，Authorization 则携带调用者的凭据。掌握这些基础，后端的其他工作都会轻松许多。
titleCn: 读懂一次 HTTP 交互

title: Designing a RESTful API
contentMd:
REST is not a strict standard but a set of useful conventions. The core idea is to treat your data as resources, each with its own URL, and to use HTTP methods as the verbs that act on them. A user becomes /users/42, and listing their orders is /users/42/orders.

A good REST API is stateless. Every request carries everything the server needs, so no session is kept between calls. This makes the system easy to scale, because any server can answer any request. It also makes failures easier to reason about.

Naming matters. Use plural nouns for collections and keep paths lowercase and nested by relationship. Avoid verbs in the path; the method already says what happens. For example, prefer POST /orders over POST /createOrder.

Finally, return the correct status codes. A created resource deserves 201, a deleted one can return 204, and a validation failure should be 422. Consistent conventions turn a messy endpoint list into a product clients enjoy using.
contentCn:
REST 不是一套严格的标准，而是一组有用的约定。它的核心思想是把数据视为资源，每个资源有自己的 URL，并用 HTTP 方法作为作用于它们的动词。一个用户就是 /users/42，列出该用户的订单则是 /users/42/orders。

一个好的 REST API 是无状态的。每个请求都携带服务器所需的全部信息，调用之间不保留会话。这让系统易于扩展，因为任何服务器都能回应任何请求，也让故障更容易推理。

命名很重要。集合用复数名词，路径保持小写并按关系嵌套。避免在路径里放动词，方法本身已经说明了动作。例如，优先使用 POST /orders 而不是 POST /createOrder。

最后，要返回正确的状态码。创建成功的资源应该给 201，删除成功可以返回 204，校验失败则应是 422。一致的约定能把杂乱的接口清单变成一个让客户端用起来舒心的产品。

title: What Status Codes Really Mean
contentMd:
Status codes are the shortest sentence a server speaks. The first digit groups the meaning: 2 for success, 3 for redirection, 4 for client errors, and 5 for server errors. Reading that digit already narrows your debugging search.

Within the 4xx family, the difference between 401 and 403 is a classic interview question. 401 says you are not logged in or your token is bad. 403 says you are logged in but not allowed. Both mean the request stopped at the door, but for different reasons.

The 5xx codes point the finger at the server. A 502 means a gateway got a bad response from an upstream service. A 504 means that upstream was too slow. A 503 often means the service is intentionally down for maintenance or overwhelmed.

Treat status codes as a contract with your clients. Document which codes each endpoint can return, and make sure your code actually sends them. A clear contract saves support tickets later.
contentCn:
状态码是服务器说出的最短的一句话。首位数字对含义做了分组：2 表示成功，3 表示重定向，4 表示客户端错误，5 表示服务器错误。读懂这个数字，就已经把你的排查范围缩小了。

在 4xx 家族里，401 和 403 的区别是一道经典面试题。401 表示你没有登录，或者你的 token 无效；403 表示你已经登录，只是没有权限。两者都意味着请求被拦在门口，只是原因不同。

5xx 则把矛头指向服务器。502 表示网关从上游服务拿到了坏响应，504 表示上游太慢，503 通常意味着服务正在维护或已被压垮。

把状态码当作与客户端的一份契约。记录清楚每个接口可能返回哪些状态码，并确保你的代码真的会发出它们。一份清晰的契约日后能省下大量支持工单。
titleCn: 状态码到底意味着什么

title: Authentication with JWT
contentMd:
When a user logs in, the server must remember who they are on later requests. One popular approach is the JSON Web Token, or JWT. After verifying the password, the server signs a small token containing the user id and roles, then sends it back to the client.

The token has three parts: a header, a payload, and a signature, joined by dots. The signature is the important part. Because the server signed it with a secret, no one can tamper with the payload without breaking the signature. The server can trust the token without a database lookup on every request.

The client stores the JWT and attaches it to the Authorization header on each call. When the token expires, a separate refresh token can fetch a new one. This split keeps short-lived access tokens safe while avoiding constant re-logins.

A common mistake is storing the token in a place JavaScript can read, which exposes it to attackers. Prefer HttpOnly cookies or careful storage, and never log the token in your backend.
contentCn:
当用户登录后，服务器必须在此后的请求中记得他是谁。一种流行的做法是 JSON Web Token，也就是 JWT。校验密码通过后，服务器签发一个包含用户 id 与角色的小 token，然后把它回传给客户端。

token 由三部分组成：header、payload 和 signature，用点号连接。其中签名是关键。因为服务器用密钥签了名，任何人改动 payload 都会让签名失效。因此服务器无需在每次请求时查一次数据库，就能信任这个 token。

客户端保存 JWT，并在每次调用时把它附加到 Authorization 头里。当 token 过期时，可以用一个单独的 refresh token 换取新的 token。这种拆分让短生命周期的 access token 更安全，同时又免去了反复登录。

一个常见错误是把 token 存在 JavaScript 能读到的地方，这会把它暴露给攻击者。请优先使用 HttpOnly cookie 或谨慎的存储方案，并且绝不要在后端日志里打印 token。
titleCn: 用 JWT 做身份认证

title: Caching to Reduce Load
contentMd:
A cache is a fast store that keeps answers to questions already asked. When a request arrives, the server checks the cache first. If the data is there and still fresh, it returns immediately without touching the database. This single trick can cut latency and cost by an enormous factor.

Cache-Control tells browsers and proxies how long to keep a response. A value like max-age=300 means the response is valid for five minutes. ETag adds a fingerprint so the client can ask, did this change? If not, the server replies 304 and saves the download.

A CDN pushes copies of static files to servers near your users around the world. Images, scripts, and stylesheets benefit the most, because they rarely change and are requested constantly.

The hard part is cache invalidation: knowing when to throw away a stale entry after a write. Many outages come from serving yesterday's data. Design your keys carefully and prefer short TTLs when correctness matters.
contentCn:
缓存是一个快速存储，专门保存那些已经被问过的问题的答案。请求到来时，服务器先查缓存，如果数据在那里而且仍然新鲜，就立刻返回，完全不碰数据库。单凭这一招，就能把延迟和成本削减一个惊人的倍数。

Cache-Control 告诉浏览器和代理应该把响应保存多久。像 max-age=300 这样的值表示响应五分钟内有效。ETag 则加上一个指纹，让客户端可以问一句：它变了吗？如果没变，服务器就回一个 304，省下下载。

CDN 会把静态文件的副本推送到世界各地靠近用户的服务器上。图片、脚本和样式表受益最大，因为它们极少变动却经常被请求。

难的是缓存失效：写入之后要知道何时丢弃陈旧的条目。许多线上事故都源于把昨天的数据发了出去。仔细设计你的 key，在正确性重要时优先选择较短的 TTL。

title: Protecting APIs with Rate Limiting
contentMd:
A public API is open to the whole internet, including buggy clients and attackers. Rate limiting is the guardrail that keeps one caller from consuming everything. It caps how many requests a key or IP may send within a window, such as a thousand per hour.

When a client exceeds the limit, the server replies with 429 Too Many Requests and often includes a Retry-After header. Polite clients read that header, wait, and try again. This backpressure keeps the system stable for everyone else.

Rate limiting also helps with cost control. Many cloud bills scale with traffic, so a runaway loop in a client's code can turn expensive fast. A limit turns that risk into a bounded, predictable number.

Pair rate limiting with good idempotency. If a client retries after being throttled, the server should not charge a card twice or create a duplicate order. The two patterns together make your API both safe and friendly.
contentCn:
一个公开 API 向整个互联网敞开，包括有 bug 的客户端和攻击者。限流是那道护栏，防止某一个调用方把所有资源都消耗掉。它限制某个 key 或 IP 在一个窗口期内能发送的请求数，比如每小时一千次。

当客户端超出限额，服务器会回复 429 Too Many Requests，并且通常会带上 Retry-After 头。有礼貌的客户端会读这个头，等待，然后重试。这种反压让系统对其他所有人保持稳定。

限流也有助于控制成本。很多云账单随流量增长，因此客户端代码里的一个死循环很快就可能烧掉一大笔钱。限流把这种风险变成一个有界、可预期的数字。

把限流和良好的幂等性搭配起来。如果客户端在被限流后重试，服务器不应重复扣款或创建重复订单。这两个模式合在一起，才让你的 API 既安全又好用。

title: Understanding CORS
contentMd:
Browsers enforce a security rule called the same-origin policy. By default, a page on one domain cannot read responses from a different domain. CORS, or Cross-Origin Resource Sharing, is the mechanism that relaxes this rule in a controlled way.

When a browser makes a cross-origin request with credentials or custom headers, it first sends a preflight. This is an OPTIONS request asking the server whether the real request is allowed. The server answers with headers such as Access-Control-Allow-Origin and Access-Control-Allow-Methods.

If those headers do not match the calling page, the browser blocks the response even though the server processed it. That surprises many beginners, because the network tab shows a 200 but the code sees an error.

The safe approach is to allow only the specific origins you trust and the methods they need. Wildcards are convenient in development but dangerous in production, especially when credentials are involved.
contentCn:
浏览器会强制执行一条叫做同源策略（same-origin policy）的安全规则。默认情况下，一个域名下的页面无法读取另一个域名的响应。CORS，也就是跨源资源共享（Cross-Origin Resource Sharing），正是一种以受控方式放宽这条规则的机制。

当浏览器发起携带凭据或自定义头的跨源请求时，它会先发送一个预检（preflight）。这是一个 OPTIONS 请求，向服务器询问真实请求是否被允许。服务器用诸如 Access-Control-Allow-Origin 和 Access-Control-Allow-Methods 这样的头部作答。

如果这些头与调用页面不匹配，即便服务器已经处理了请求，浏览器依然会拦截响应。这让许多新手感到意外，因为网络面板里显示的是 200，而代码里看到的却是错误。

安全的做法是只允许你信任的具体来源以及它们真正需要的方法。通配符在开发时很方便，但在生产环境很危险，尤其当涉及凭据时。

title: Reacting with Webhooks
contentMd:
Most APIs are request-driven: a client asks, and the server answers. Webhooks turn this around. Instead of polling, you register a URL, and the server calls it when something interesting happens, such as a payment clearing or a build finishing.

A webhook is just an HTTP POST to your URL with a JSON body describing the event. Your endpoint should accept it quickly, acknowledge with 200, and process the work in the background. Taking too long risks timeouts and duplicate deliveries.

Because the internet is unreliable, webhooks may arrive more than once. Design your handler to be idempotent, so receiving the same event twice has no extra effect. Storing a seen-event id is a simple way to do this.

Security matters. Anyone who knows the URL could post fake events. Verify a signature header, or keep the endpoint behind a secret path, so you only trust messages the sender really produced.
contentCn:
大多数 API 都是请求驱动的：客户端提问，服务器作答。Webhook 把这个关系倒过来。你不必轮询，而是注册一个 URL，当有值得关注的事情发生时，服务器会来调用它，比如一笔支付完成清算或一次构建结束。

Webhook 就是一次发往你 URL 的 HTTP POST，请求体是描述该事件的 JSON。你的接口应该尽快接收，用 200 确认，然后把工作放到后台处理。耗时太长会带来超时和重复投递的风险。

由于互联网并不可靠，Webhook 可能到达不止一次。设计处理逻辑时务必保持幂等，让同一个事件收到两次也不会产生额外影响。保存一个已处理事件 id 是最简单的做法。

安全性同样重要。任何知道该 URL 的人都可以伪造事件。请校验签名头，或者把接口藏在一个带密钥的路径之后，这样你只信任真正由发送方产生的消息。

title: Building Reliable Backends
contentMd:
A backend that works in the lab can still fail in production, where networks drop and disks fill. Reliability is the craft of expecting those failures and degrading gracefully instead of collapsing.

Timeouts bound how long you wait for a dependency. Without one, a single slow database can hang every request and exhaust your threads. Retries let you survive brief blips, but always add backoff and jitter so many clients do not retry at the exact same instant.

The circuit breaker pattern stops calling a service that is clearly unhealthy. After a number of failures, it opens and fails fast, giving the dependency time to recover. Later it tests with a single call before fully closing.

Health checks let a load balancer route traffic only to ready nodes. Combined with good logging and alerts, these patterns turn unpredictable outages into manageable, observable incidents.
contentCn:
在实验环境里跑得好好的后端，上线后仍可能失灵，因为那里网络会掉、磁盘会满。可靠性这门手艺，就是预料到这些故障并优雅降级，而不是直接崩溃。

超时（timeout）限定了你等待依赖的时长。没有超时，一个缓慢的数据库就能挂起所有请求并耗尽你的线程。重试让你能挺过短暂的抖动，但一定要加上退避和抖动，免得许多客户端在同一瞬间一起重试。

熔断器模式会停止调用一个明显不健康的服务。失败达到一定次数后，熔断器打开并快速失败，给依赖留出恢复时间。之后它会先用一次调用试探，再完全闭合。

健康检查让负载均衡器只把流量导向就绪的节点。配合良好的日志与告警，这些模式能把不可预测的故障变成可管理、可观测的事件。

title: Scaling a Backend
contentMd:
As usage grows, a single server stops being enough. Scaling is the work of serving more traffic without slowing down or breaking. There are two broad directions: make one machine stronger, or add more machines.

Horizontal scaling, the more common choice, means running several identical instances behind a load balancer. The balancer spreads requests so no instance is overloaded, and if one crashes, the others keep serving. Stateless services scale this way almost for free.

A message queue helps here too. When a task is slow, like sending emails, put it on a queue and let a worker handle it later. The web server answers fast, and the background job catches up at its own pace.

Caching and a CDN remove load before it reaches your app. Together, these techniques let a small team serve millions of users by adding capacity where the bottleneck actually lives.
contentCn:
随着使用量增长，单台服务器就不够用了。扩展就是要在不减速、不出故障的前提下服务更多流量。大方向有两个：把一台机器变得更强，或者增加更多机器。

水平扩展是更常见的选择，意味着一台负载均衡器后面跑若干完全相同的实例。均衡器把请求摊开，不让任何实例过载；某个实例崩溃时，其余的继续服务。无状态服务几乎可以零成本地这样扩展。

消息队列在这里同样有用。当某个任务很慢，比如发送邮件，就把它放进队列，让 worker 稍后处理。Web 服务器可以快速响应，后台任务则按自己的节奏慢慢追上。

缓存和 CDN 能在负载到达你的应用之前就把它卸掉。这些技术合在一起，让一个小团队也能通过在真正的瓶颈处增加容量来服务数百万用户。

title: REST versus RPC for Service APIs
contentMd:
REST models an API around resources and the standard HTTP verbs, while RPC models it around actions you can invoke. Choosing between them is a common design interview question.

REST maps well to public, long-lived APIs. Clients already understand caching, status codes, and idempotency, and a resource-oriented model stays stable as the data grows. The cost is that complex operations do not always fit neatly into create, read, update, and delete, so you end up designing artificial resources or overloading a POST endpoint.

RPC, especially over gRPC, shines for internal service-to-service calls where you want strongly typed contracts, streaming, and low latency from binary serialization. The trade-off is weaker caching and a contract that couples caller and callee more tightly. A practical answer: expose REST at the edge for external consumers, and use RPC internally where performance and typed contracts matter most.
contentCn:
REST 围绕资源与标准 HTTP 动词来建模 API，而 RPC 围绕「可调用的动作」来建模。如何在两者之间选择，是常见的设计面试题。

REST 很适合对外、长期演进的 API。客户端天然理解缓存、状态码与幂等性，而且面向资源的模型在数据结构增长时依然稳定。代价在于：复杂操作往往无法整齐地塞进增删改查里，于是你不得不造出一些人为的「资源」，或者让某个 POST 端点承担过多语义。

RPC（尤其是 gRPC）在内部服务间调用中更有优势：强类型契约、流式传输，以及二进制序列化带来的低延迟。代价是缓存能力较弱，且契约会把调用方与被调用方耦合得更紧。务实的回答是：对外用 REST 暴露给外部消费者，内部在性能与强类型契约更重要的地方使用 RPC。
titleEn: REST versus RPC for Service APIs
titleCn: 服务 API 中的 REST 与 RPC 之争

title: Strategies for API Versioning
contentMd:
Every public API eventually changes, and versioning decides how existing clients survive that change. The three common strategies are URL versioning, header versioning, and content negotiation.

URL versioning, such as a path prefix, is the most explicit and easiest to cache, debug, and route, which is why most public APIs use it. Header versioning keeps URLs clean and lets you version a single resource independently, but it is invisible in logs and harder to test by hand. Content negotiation using a custom media type is the most purist approach and the most cumbersome in practice.

Whichever you choose, the deeper advice interviewers look for is to avoid versioning altogether when you can: add optional fields rather than changing existing ones, never remove or repurpose a field, and treat every response field as a permanent contract. Version only for genuinely breaking changes, and always publish a deprecation window so clients have time to migrate.
contentCn:
任何公开 API 最终都会变化，而版本化策略决定了现有客户端能否扛过这次变化。常见有三种：URL 版本化、请求头版本化、以及内容协商。

URL 版本化（例如路径前缀）最直观，也最容易缓存、调试和路由，因此绝大多数公开 API 都采用它。请求头版本化能让 URL 保持干净，并支持对单个资源独立版本化，但它在日志里不可见，手工测试也更麻烦。使用自定义媒体类型做内容协商是最纯粹的做法，实践中也最繁琐。

无论选哪种，面试官更想听到的深层建议是：能不加版本就不加——新增可选字段而不要改动既有字段，绝不删除或改变字段含义，把每个响应字段都当作永久契约。只有真正破坏性的变更才引入新版本，并且一定要公布废弃窗口，给客户端留出迁移时间。

title: Offset versus Cursor Pagination
contentMd:
Listing a large collection requires pagination, and the two dominant approaches behave very differently at scale. Offset pagination uses a page number and size, while cursor pagination uses an opaque pointer to a position in the result set.

Offset pagination is simple and lets users jump to any page, but it degrades as the offset grows because the database must scan and discard every skipped row. It also produces duplicates and gaps when new rows are inserted while a user pages through results.

Cursor pagination encodes the last seen sort key, so the query seeks directly to that position and stays fast regardless of depth. It handles concurrent inserts gracefully and is the right choice for feeds, logs, and infinite scroll. The trade-off is that you cannot jump to an arbitrary page. Strong answers mention keyset pagination on a stable, unique sort column, and note that offsets remain acceptable for small, mostly static admin lists.
contentCn:
列出一个大型集合必须分页，而两种主流做法在规模变大时表现截然不同。偏移量分页使用页码与每页条数，游标分页则使用一个指向结果集位置的不透明指针。

偏移量分页实现简单，还允许用户跳到任意页；但随着偏移量增大，它性能会明显下降，因为数据库必须扫描并丢弃所有被跳过的行。此外，当用户在翻页过程中有新数据插入时，它还会产生重复和遗漏。

游标分页把「上一页最后一条的排序键」编码进游标，查询可以直接定位到该位置，无论翻多深都保持快速。它能优雅地处理并发插入，是信息流、日志和无限滚动场景的正确选择。代价是无法跳到任意页。出色的回答会提到：在一个稳定且唯一的排序列上做 keyset 分页；同时指出对于规模小、基本静态的后台列表，偏移量分页仍然可以接受。
titleCn: 偏移量分页与游标分页

title: Rate Limiting Algorithms Compared
contentMd:
Rate limiting protects a service from abuse and from its own clients. The four algorithms interviewers ask about are fixed window, sliding window, token bucket, and leaky bucket.

A fixed window counter is trivial to implement but allows twice the limit at a window boundary, since a burst can land at the end of one window and the start of the next. Sliding window logging fixes that by tracking timestamps, at the cost of more memory. A token bucket refills tokens at a steady rate and lets a caller burst up to the bucket capacity, which matches most real traffic nicely. A leaky bucket processes requests at a constant rate and smooths bursts into a queue.

In practice, token bucket is the default choice because it permits short bursts while enforcing a sustained average. Also mention where to enforce it: at the gateway for coarse protection, and per user or API key rather than globally, so one noisy client cannot starve everyone else. Always return a retry-after header.
contentCn:
限流用于保护服务免受滥用，也防止被自家客户端拖垮。面试官常问的四种算法是：固定窗口、滑动窗口、令牌桶和漏桶。

固定窗口计数器实现最简单，但在窗口边界处会放过两倍流量，因为一波突发可以分别落在上一个窗口末尾和下一个窗口开头。滑动窗口日志通过记录时间戳解决了这个问题，代价是占用更多内存。令牌桶以稳定速率补充令牌，允许调用方突发到桶容量上限，这与真实流量形态相当契合。漏桶则以恒定速率处理请求，把突发削平成队列。

实践中令牌桶是默认选择，因为它既允许短时突发，又能强制执行长期平均速率。还应该说明在哪里执行限流：在网关层做粗粒度保护；并且按用户或 API 密钥限流，而不是全局限流，这样一个吵闹的客户端就无法饿死其他所有人。同时务必返回 retry-after 响应头。

title: JWT versus Server Sessions
contentMd:
Authentication state can live on the server in a session or inside a signed token the client carries. Understanding the trade-off is a staple interview question.

A server session stores state in a shared store and sends only an opaque identifier in a cookie. The server can revoke access instantly, which matters for logout and incident response, but every request needs a lookup and the store becomes a scaling concern.

A JWT carries claims inside a signed token, so any service can verify it without a database call, which suits stateless microservices. The catch is revocation: a token stays valid until it expires, so you need short lifetimes plus a refresh token, or a denylist for urgent cases. Also note that JWTs are signed, not encrypted, so never put secrets in the payload. A balanced answer recommends sessions for traditional web apps and short-lived JWTs for service-to-service or mobile flows.
contentCn:
认证状态可以存放在服务端会话里，也可以放在客户端携带的签名令牌里。理解这个取舍是经典面试题。

服务端会话把状态存在共享存储中，只通过 Cookie 下发一个不透明标识符。服务器可以即时吊销访问权限，这对登出和安全事件响应至关重要；但每个请求都需要一次查询，这个存储也成了扩展时的负担。

JWT 把声明信息放进签名令牌内部，任何服务都能直接校验而不必查库，非常适合无状态的微服务。麻烦在于吊销：令牌在过期前一直有效，因此你需要较短的有效期配合刷新令牌，或在紧急情况下维护一份拒绝名单。还要注意到 JWT 是签名而非加密的，绝不能把机密放进载荷。一个平衡的回答是：传统 Web 应用用会话，服务间调用或移动端流程用短生命周期的 JWT。

title: Implementing Graceful Shutdown
contentMd:
A deployment that kills processes mid-request produces errors for users even when the new version is healthy. Graceful shutdown is how you avoid that.

The pattern has three steps. First, stop accepting new work: deregister from the load balancer or fail the readiness probe so traffic drains before the process exits. Second, let in-flight requests finish, bounded by a timeout so a stuck request cannot hold the process forever. Third, release resources explicitly: close database connections, flush buffers, and finish or requeue in-progress messages.

In Java and Spring, a shutdown hook plus a configurable server shutdown period handles most of this, but you must also make thread pools and message listeners cooperate by waiting for submitted tasks. Mention that the readiness probe should fail before the liveness probe does, and that a hard kill timeout should always exist as a last resort so a deploy never hangs indefinitely.
contentCn:
如果部署时把进程直接杀掉，正在处理的请求就会失败，即便新版本本身是健康的。优雅关闭正是为了避免这种情况。

这个模式分三步。第一，停止接收新工作：从负载均衡摘除，或让就绪探针失败，使流量在进程退出前先排空。第二，让进行中的请求处理完，并用超时兜底，避免某个卡住的请求永久拖住进程。第三，显式释放资源：关闭数据库连接、刷新缓冲区、完成或重新入队正在处理的消息。

在 Java 与 Spring 中，关闭钩子加上可配置的服务器关闭等待期能覆盖大部分场景；但你还必须让线程池和消息监听器配合，等待已提交的任务结束。还应提到：就绪探针应当比存活探针更早失败，并且始终要有一个强制终止超时作为最后手段，保证部署永远不会无限挂起。

title: Sizing a Database Connection Pool
contentMd:
Opening a database connection is expensive, so applications keep a pool of reusable connections. Getting the size wrong is one of the most common production performance mistakes.

Bigger is not better. A database can only execute a limited number of queries in parallel, bounded by its cores and disk; adding more concurrent connections mostly increases context switching and lock contention, and latency climbs while throughput stays flat. Many teams discover that a pool of twenty outperforms a pool of two hundred on the same hardware.

A sensible starting point is roughly the number of database cores times two, plus headroom for short spikes, then measure and adjust. Also set a connection timeout so callers fail fast rather than piling up, and monitor wait time; growing wait time with stable query time means the pool, not the database, is the bottleneck. Remember that the effective limit is pool size multiplied by the number of application instances.
contentCn:
建立数据库连接开销很大，因此应用会维护一个可复用的连接池。把连接池大小配错是最常见的生产性能问题之一。

并不是越大越好。数据库能并行执行的查询数量有限，受限于 CPU 核数与磁盘；增加更多并发连接多半只是带来更多上下文切换与锁竞争，延迟上升而吞吐持平。很多团队会发现，在同样硬件上，二十个连接的池子表现优于两百个连接的池子。

合理的起点大约是数据库核数乘以二，再为短时突发留些余量，然后实测调整。同时设置连接超时，让调用方快速失败而不是无限堆积；并监控等待时间——如果等待时间持续增长而查询耗时稳定，说明瓶颈在连接池而不是数据库。还要记住：实际的上限是连接池大小乘以应用实例数。
titleCn: 数据库连接池的容量规划

title: Fixing the N+1 Query Problem
contentMd:
The N+1 query problem happens when code runs one query to fetch a list and then one additional query per row to fetch related data. A page showing fifty orders suddenly issues fifty-one queries.

It usually hides behind lazy loading in an ORM. Accessing a relationship inside a loop triggers a fresh query each iteration, and everything looks fine in development with three rows. The fix is to fetch the related data eagerly, either with a join, a batched second query using the collected ids, or an explicit fetch join the ORM supports.

Detection matters as much as the fix. Enable query logging in development, assert on the number of queries in tests, and watch for a query whose text repeats dozens of times in production logs. Also mention that batching trades a small increase in memory for a large reduction in round trips, and that entity graphs should be tuned per use case rather than globally eager.
contentCn:
N+1 查询问题指的是：代码先执行一条查询拿到列表，然后为每一行再执行一条查询去取关联数据。一个展示五十条订单的页面，瞬间就发出了五十一条查询。

它通常藏在 ORM 的懒加载背后。在循环里访问关联关系会为每次迭代触发一次新查询，而在开发环境只有三行数据时一切看起来都很正常。修复方式是提前把关联数据取出来：可以用 join、用收集到的 id 做一次批量二次查询，或者使用 ORM 支持的显式 fetch join。

发现问题与修复同样重要。在开发环境开启查询日志，在测试中断言查询次数，并在生产日志里留意那些重复出现几十次的相同语句。还应提到：批量查询是用少量内存增长换来网络往返的大幅减少；而且实体图的加载策略应当按具体用例调优，而不是全局改成急加载。
titleCn: 修复 N+1 查询问题

title: Optimistic versus Pessimistic Locking
contentMd:
When two transactions might modify the same row, you must choose how to protect it. Optimistic and pessimistic locking are the two answers.

Pessimistic locking takes a database lock before reading, so conflicting writers block until the holder commits. It is correct and simple under heavy contention, but it holds locks across the transaction, reduces throughput, and risks deadlocks if lock order is inconsistent.

Optimistic locking adds a version column and checks it on update: if the version changed since you read, someone else won and you retry or fail. It avoids holding locks and scales far better when conflicts are rare, which is the common case. Choose optimistic locking for most business updates, fall back to pessimistic locking when contention is genuinely high, and always make the update conditional in a single statement so the check and write cannot race.
contentCn:
当两个事务可能修改同一行时，你必须决定如何保护它。乐观锁与悲观锁是两种答案。

悲观锁在读取前就获取数据库锁，冲突的写操作会阻塞，直到持锁者提交。在高冲突场景下它正确且简单，但它会在整个事务期间持有锁，压低吞吐，并且若加锁顺序不一致还存在死锁风险。

乐观锁增加一个版本列，并在更新时校验：如果版本自你读取后已变化，说明别人先成功了，你就重试或失败。它不持有锁，在冲突罕见的场景下扩展性远好于悲观锁——而这正是常见情况。对多数业务更新选用乐观锁；当冲突确实很高时回退到悲观锁；并且始终在单条语句里完成条件更新，使校验与写入之间无法产生竞态。

title: What an API Gateway Does
contentMd:
An API gateway is the single entry point that sits in front of many backend services. Clients talk to one host, and the gateway handles cross-cutting concerns so individual services do not have to.

Typical responsibilities include routing a path to the right service, authenticating tokens, enforcing rate limits, terminating TLS, and aggregating several backend calls into one response for mobile clients. Centralizing these concerns removes duplicated code and gives you one place to add logging and metrics.

The risk is turning the gateway into a bottleneck or a monolith of business logic. Keep it thin: routing and infrastructure policies belong there, business orchestration does not. Also mention that a gateway adds a hop, so measure its added latency, and that it must be highly available because every request depends on it.
contentCn:
API 网关是位于众多后端服务之前的统一入口。客户端只与一个主机通信，由网关处理各类横切关注点，各个服务因此不必重复实现。

典型职责包括：把路径路由到正确的服务、校验令牌、执行限流、终结 TLS，以及为移动端把多个后端调用聚合为一次响应。把这些关注点集中起来，既消除了重复代码，也给出了统一添加日志与指标的位置。

风险在于把网关变成瓶颈，或者演化成塞满业务逻辑的巨石。要保持它轻薄：路由和基础设施策略属于网关，业务编排不属于。还应提到网关会增加一跳网络开销，因此要测量它带来的额外延迟；同时它必须高可用，因为每个请求都要经过它。

title: The Bulkhead Pattern
contentMd:
The bulkhead pattern takes its name from ship compartments: if one floods, the others keep the vessel afloat. In software it means partitioning resources so failure in one area cannot consume everything.

Concretely, you give each downstream dependency its own thread pool, connection pool, or semaphore. If the reporting service becomes slow, only the reporting pool saturates, and checkout continues to work because it never shared those threads. Without isolation, one slow dependency exhausts a shared pool and takes down unrelated features.

The trade-off is that partitioning reduces overall utilization, since idle capacity in one pool cannot be borrowed by another. Choose boundaries by failure domain rather than by team, size each pool from measurement, and combine the pattern with timeouts and circuit breakers. Interviewers like the observation that bulkheads, timeouts, and circuit breakers solve three different problems and are most effective together.
contentCn:
舱壁模式得名于船体隔舱：一个隔舱进水，其余隔舱仍能保住船不沉。在软件中，它指的是对资源进行分区，使某一处的故障无法吞噬全部资源。

具体做法是：给每个下游依赖分配独立的线程池、连接池或信号量。如果报表服务变慢，只有报表专用的池子会被占满，而结账流程依然可用，因为它从未共用那些线程。若不做隔离，一个变慢的依赖会耗尽共享池，进而拖垮与之无关的功能。

代价是分区会降低整体利用率，因为某个池子闲置的容量无法借给另一个池子使用。边界应按故障域而非团队来划分，每个池子的大小依据实测确定，并与超时、熔断器配合使用。面试官会欣赏这样的观察：舱壁、超时和熔断器解决的是三个不同的问题，三者结合才最有效。

title: How CORS Actually Works
contentMd:
Cross-origin resource sharing is a browser security rule, not a server one. A server can be perfectly healthy and still see requests blocked because the browser refused to hand the response to JavaScript.

The rule is the same-origin policy: a script may read a response only if scheme, host, and port match. To allow otherwise, the server returns headers naming the permitted origins, methods, and headers. For requests that are not simple, such as those with a JSON content type or a custom header, the browser first sends a preflight OPTIONS request and only sends the real request if the server approves.

Two points interviewers probe. Credentials require an explicit allow-credentials header and cannot be combined with a wildcard origin. And because CORS is enforced by the browser, tools like curl and server-to-server calls are unaffected, which is why a failing API often works when tested from the command line.
contentCn:
跨源资源共享（CORS）是一条浏览器安全规则，而不是服务端规则。服务端可能完全健康，但请求依然被拦截，因为浏览器拒绝把响应交给 JavaScript。

这条规则就是同源策略：只有当协议、主机和端口都一致时，脚本才能读取响应。若要放开限制，服务端需要返回响应头，声明允许的来源、方法与请求头。对于非简单请求（例如使用 JSON 内容类型或自定义请求头），浏览器会先发送一个 OPTIONS 预检请求，只有服务端批准后才发送真正的请求。

面试官常追问两点。携带凭证需要显式的 allow-credentials 响应头，且不能与通配来源同时使用。另外，由于 CORS 由浏览器强制执行，curl 之类的工具和服务端之间的调用不受影响——这就是为什么一个失败的 API 在命令行里测试却往往是正常的。

title: Choosing Timeouts for Remote Calls
contentMd:
Every call to another service, database, or cache needs a timeout. Without one, a slow dependency quietly consumes your threads until the whole service stops responding.

Timeouts must be chosen deliberately rather than left at defaults. A connect timeout should be short, since establishing a connection either succeeds quickly or the host is unreachable. A read timeout should reflect the dependency's realistic tail latency, ideally derived from its p99 rather than its average, because an average-based timeout rejects a meaningful fraction of legitimate requests.

Also set a deadline for the entire user request so retries and fan-out cannot exceed it, and make the timeout budget shrink as the call descends the stack: the outermost handler has the most time, each nested call strictly less. Pair timeouts with a circuit breaker so repeated failures fail fast instead of waiting out the timer on every request.
contentCn:
每一次调用其他服务、数据库或缓存都必须设置超时。没有超时，一个变慢的依赖会悄悄耗尽你的线程，直到整个服务停止响应。

超时必须刻意设定，而不是沿用默认值。连接超时应较短，因为建连要么很快成功，要么目标不可达。读取超时应反映依赖真实的尾部延迟，最好依据其 p99 而非平均值来设定——因为基于平均值的超时会拒绝掉相当一部分合法请求。

此外还要为整个用户请求设定截止时间，使重试与扇出调用都无法突破它；并让超时预算随调用栈下沉而递减：最外层处理器时间最多，每一层嵌套调用严格更少。把超时与熔断器配合使用，使重复失败能快速失败，而不必每个请求都干等计时器走完。

title: Retries with Exponential Backoff
contentMd:
Transient failures are normal in distributed systems, so retrying is natural. But naive retries turn a small outage into a much larger one.

Retrying immediately in a tight loop adds load exactly when the downstream service is already struggling, which can push it from degraded to dead. Exponential backoff fixes this by doubling the wait between attempts, and adding randomized jitter prevents many clients from retrying in lockstep and recreating the thundering herd.

Two more rules matter. Only retry idempotent operations, or make them idempotent with a key, otherwise a retry may duplicate a payment. And cap both the number of attempts and the total elapsed time, since a client that retries forever is worse than one that fails fast. Skip retrying on errors that will never succeed, such as a validation failure, and let the circuit breaker stop traffic once failure rates cross a threshold.
contentCn:
在分布式系统里，瞬时失败很常见，因此重试是自然反应。但朴素的重试会把一次小故障放大成一场大故障。

在紧密循环里立即重试，恰好会在下游服务已经苦苦支撑时继续加压，可能把它从「降级」直接推到「崩溃」。指数退避通过在每次尝试之间成倍延长等待时间来解决这个问题；再叠加随机抖动，可以避免大量客户端步调一致地重试、重新制造出惊群效应。

还有两条规则很重要。只重试幂等操作，或者用幂等键把它变成幂等的，否则一次重试就可能造成重复扣款。同时限制重试次数与总耗时，因为无限重试的客户端比快速失败的客户端更糟。对那些永远不会成功的错误（如参数校验失败）不要重试；当失败率越过阈值后，交给熔断器直接切断流量。

title: Readiness and Liveness Probes
contentMd:
Orchestrators need to know whether to send traffic to an instance and whether to restart it. Those are two different questions, which is why readiness and liveness probes are separate.

A readiness probe asks can this instance serve right now. Failing it removes the instance from the load balancer without killing it, which is what you want during startup, during a graceful shutdown, or when a required dependency is temporarily unavailable.

A liveness probe asks is this process broken beyond recovery. Failing it triggers a restart, so it must only depend on the process itself and never on external systems; a liveness probe that checks the database will restart every instance during a database outage and make things dramatically worse. Keep liveness shallow, make readiness reflect real dependencies, and add a startup probe for slow-booting services so they are not killed before they finish initializing.
contentCn:
编排系统需要知道：该不该把流量发给这个实例，以及要不要重启它。这是两个不同的问题，因此就绪探针与存活探针必须分开。

就绪探针问的是「这个实例现在能不能提供服务」。失败时，编排系统会把实例从负载均衡中摘除而不是杀死它——这正是启动过程中、优雅关闭期间，或某个必需依赖临时不可用时所期望的行为。

存活探针问的是「这个进程是否已经坏到无法恢复」。失败会触发重启，因此它只能依赖进程自身，绝不能依赖外部系统；一个会去检查数据库的存活探针，会在数据库故障期间重启所有实例，让情况急剧恶化。做法要点是：存活探针保持轻量，就绪探针反映真实依赖，并为启动较慢的服务增加启动探针，避免它们在初始化完成前就被杀掉。
